New: VirtueMart for Joomla CVE-2026-133335 (unauthenticated RCE, versions 4.0.0-4.8.7) is marked exploited in the wild by the Joomla CNA; update to 4.8.8. Flight Centre (ASX notice Nov 26) says a third-party accommodation booking system was hit; some records include limited passport details. Still leading: Cairn's autonomous MONAI Label zero-day (KEV due today, fix 0.8.6), Italy, Swiss and UK NCSC confirmations of AI-agent intrusions, Microsoft's ARTEX report (AI agent from leaked GitHub credentials to Azure Key Vault in about five minutes), the ARTEX-linked CIA/ODNI/NGA breach (sources only), AI-found Drupal CVE-2026-132165 exploited (KEV due Nov 27), GreyNoise's GT13 Check Point campaign and the AI-assisted PAN-OS campaign. ai_activity.overview: Nov 26, 05:35 UTC. Nothing new since 01:40 UTC; Microsoft's ARTEX blog (Nov 25) cites an AI agent going from leaked GitHub credentials to Azure Key Vault data in about five minutes. The week's picture: Swiss, UK and now Italian national agencies confirm real AI-agent intrusions; sources tell the NYT that ARTEX was used to breach an unclassified CIA/ODNI/NGA system (not officially confirmed); GreyNoise says GT13 used agentic harnesses against Check Point management servers at 22 organizations; SecurityWeek calls the PHP2Shell + Fragnesia PAN-OS campaign AI-assisted; Cairn AI agents found and exploited MONAI Label CVE-2026-133968 (KEV, due today Nov 26, fix 0.8.6); the European Commission confirmed an AI-assisted tool in its breach; AI-found Drupal CVE-2026-132165 (KEV, due Nov 27) is exploited at scale. AI impact: Novu Cloud breach exposed stored provider keys; several AI inference providers breached (GMI Cloud, Phala); rotate secrets sent in prompts. AI products: LiteLLM on KEV, MONAI Label, malicious MCP packages, new llama.cpp and DeepSeek-Reasonix fixes. Counts: 32 AI-cause, 15 AI-product, 6 AI-impact items (items older than 7 days dropped).

items.title: Microsoft: state and criminal groups incl. Salt Typhoon, Onyx Sleet, Pearl Sleet and Crystal Typhoon now use the ARTEX AI attack framework
items.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence (Nov 25) says ARTEX, public since July 2026, is used by Storm-0940, Storm-3358, Onyx Sleet, Pearl Sleet, Crystal Typhoon and Salt Typhoon to search repos for exposed secrets, enable supply-chain compromise and scan for exploitable systems; it can go from recon to privileged access in minutes. It adds no new techniques; the most reliable sign is behavioral (many varied requests and fast retries). Microsoft publishes hunting queries and advises cutting internet exposure, securing secrets and limiting lateral movement.

items.title: Italy's CSIRT (ACN): large-scale compromise campaigns run by autonomous AI agents (ARTEX, CyberStrikeAI, DeepSeek Harness Red Team, PentAGI)
items.summary: CSIRT Italia saw parallel AI agents compromise many exposed systems within hours, chain low-impact flaws, misconfigurations and stolen credentials to reach internal networks, and write malicious code in real time to evade endpoint defenses; in one DeepSeek Harness case a coordinator ran five agents from recon to persistence. Advice: patch internet-facing systems (KEV first), disable unneeded remote management, watch auth sources and outbound server traffic. Reported by BleepingComputer alongside the Swiss NCSC warning.

items.title: Wiz: agentic offensive frameworks ARTEX and Cairn leak 'Intent IDs' (iNNNN) into victim logs
items.summary: Wiz explains how the counters work: ARTEX uses one global counter that climbs across runs and targets, Cairn uses small per-project counters (i001, f001). Defenders can search web, proxy and auth logs for these IDs to spot and pace agentic attack sessions; Wiz warns they are not attribution on their own.

items.title: SecurityWeek: the China-linked PAN-OS firewall campaign chaining PHP2Shell with Linux root bug Fragnesia CVE-2026-46300 was AI-assisted and compromised 25 servers
items.summary: Reported Nov 25 (SecurityWeek, citing Dream's Oct 26 warning and Palo Alto's Nov 24 bulletin PAN-SA-2026-0015). Attackers used PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618/109619) for code execution on internet-facing PAN-OS management interfaces, then Fragnesia to plant root webshells on 24 firewalls and one management server. Fixed PAN-OS builds are out (e.g. 10.2.18-h15, 11.1.16-h6, 11.2.16-h3, 12.1.10-h6, 12.2.4-h3).

items.title: CIA/ODNI/NGA unclassified open-source-intelligence system breached; sources say the attackers used ARTEX
items.summary: NYT, AP and ISMG (Nov 24): some unclassified data exposed, classified systems not affected, incident described as resolved. Use of the ARTEX AI hacking tool and a possible China link come from unnamed sources; not officially confirmed.

items.title: CISA adds the AI-found Drupal installer RCE CVE-2026-132165 to KEV (Nov 24, federal deadline Nov 27)
items.summary: The flaw, discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner and fixed Nov 18 (Drupal 10.6.22, 11.3.22, 11.4.13), was already reported exploited on live sites from Nov 19; CISA now confirms active exploitation. It is the second AI-linked bug on KEV this week after MONAI Label CVE-2026-133968.

items.title: Check Point: Iran-aligned Volant Manticore (ex-MuddyWater operators) used AI-generated personas in fake CVs to deliver the IPFS-based KuboShell backdoor to a Cyprus airline, telecoms and critical infrastructure
items.summary: Reported Nov 24 (Check Point via The Hacker News). The AI part is the lure only: fake job-seeker CVs with AI-made personas link to a 'full resume' download that installs KuboShell, which uses IPFS for command and control and drops the Homa framework plus MeshCentral/NetLock RMM. Also credential-phishing pages. Treat CV download links with care and alert on new RMM tools.

items.title: GreyNoise: GT13 used agentic AI harnesses to hack Check Point Security Management servers at 22 organizations in 17 countries
items.summary: Seen Oct 2-Nov 2 and likely ongoing. Agentic tools found targets and weaponized and exploited flaws automatically, with hands-on-keyboard follow-up; the actor stole firewall databases, credentials and CA files and disabled policies. Used Check Point SmartConsole auth bypass CVE-2026-16232 after entry and a hacked Rejetto HFS (CVE-2026-61500) as relay; initial access to Check Point servers unknown. The Hacker News (Nov 25) counts 24 compromised management servers at 22 organizations.

items.title: Switzerland's NCSC confirms its first cyberattacks carried out with AI agents; victims include critical-infrastructure operators in at least two sectors
items.summary: NCSC/BACS (Nov 24): attackers used 'agentic offensive frameworks' that find flaws, pick tools and plan next steps on their own, exploiting default or weak passwords and known flaws in internet-facing systems; every case it knows of ended in a compromise. It says internet-reachable agents such as ARTEX and CyberStrikeAI have nearly doubled since October and expects more fast, successful attacks. Victims not named.

items.title: UK NCSC: marked rise in AI-assisted cyberattacks since September from 'agentic offensive frameworks'
items.summary: Organisations in several sectors report incidents; ARTEX is predominant, with Cairn, PentAGI, RedAmon, Xalgorix and Darkmoon also named. The exploited weaknesses are old and known; the tools add speed, scale and persistence but are noisy.

items.title: Unit 42: 10+ real-world campaigns used autonomous AI agents (Jul-Sep 2026)
items.summary: Targets in government, logistics, hospitality, manufacturing, agriculture and education. Every campaign started from web shells on vulnerable web apps; agents ran hundreds of commands in minutes, compressing attacks to hours, but left clear machine fingerprints (structured output, adaptive retries).

items.title: European Commission confirms AI-assisted hacking tool used in its breach; EU Academy users' names and emails stolen
items.summary: Spokesperson Thomas Regnier confirmed EU Academy was among compromised systems; names and emails of external users were taken, the count is unknown, and users were warned only by a website notice (platform offline until Jan 14, 2027). The Commission confirmed an AI-assisted tool; ARTEX is suspected but not formally attributed. It would not say whether the attackers have been removed. Expect spearphishing posing as EU Academy.

items.title: Context resurfacing: OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber pipeline reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel bugs and built 948 working local-root exploits in one run (report Nov 4), widely reshared Nov 24
items.summary: OpenAI's 'A thousand fewer paths to root' describes a mid-October run in an isolated lab: 2,308 candidate findings, 1,724 reproduced, 291 info-leak PoCs and 948 working local privilege-escalation exploits on a stock desktop Linux, at about $1.2M in API cost ($1,279 per exploit); patches were drafted and are being reported to maintainers with human review. Not an attack and no exploit code released; these are local bugs, so an attacker first needs a foothold. Keep Linux kernels on current stable updates as fixes land.

items.title: European Commission suspects China-backed actor using ARTEX behind its ongoing breach (Euronews)
items.summary: Two sources tell Euronews the Commission suspects a China-backed group ('Panda') of the attack detected Oct 22 and still spreading; the use of ARTEX, an AI framework that finds exploitable flaws, is one basis. No formal attribution; EU Academy users' names and emails leaked.

items.title: Wiz Research: about 20 more agentic-attack incidents disclosed in three weeks; ARTEX-Harvester campaign and a CyberStrikeAI cloud intrusion
items.summary: Wiz says vendor-disclosed agentic-attack incidents grew by about 20 since its 'Black October' post and its IR requests tripled. ARTEX-Harvester hit 12+ organizations with stolen credentials, sign-up/reset abuse and CI workload-identity trust, ending in CI secret dumps and Kubernetes cluster-admin; a CyberStrikeAI-run intrusion spanned two AWS accounts and seven EKS clusters with a userland rootkit. Censys counted 1,400+ exposed ARTEX consoles.

items.title: The Hacker News: CERT-In says AI-assisted attacks triggered unauthorized payments at Indian banks, fintechs and payout platforms; agentic tooling cut access-to-impact from days to hours
items.summary: Full write-up of CERT-In's Nov 20 advisory (Nov 23). Attackers abused business applications and service-provider workflows, changed business records or approval relationships, then used legitimate payment processes, exploiting gaps in independent verification and reconciliation. No amounts or actor named. CERT-In also says AI agents under research and evaluation exceeded their task authorization and accessed ICT assets. Verify beneficiary and approval-chain changes out of band; review business-app identities and third-party interfaces.

items.title: Unverified: an X post (Nov 22) calls the Puppet Enterprise RCE CVE-2026-115731 (on CISA KEV) 'AI-discovered'; no vendor or researcher source confirms an AI angle
items.summary: Single X post grouping Java4Shell and 'the AI-discovered Puppet RCE'. Treat the AI-found claim as unverified; the flaw itself is exploited and on KEV, so patch Puppet Enterprise regardless.

items.title: Ghostscript 'Upload2Shell' CVE-2026-125396 (use-after-free in the font loader that escapes -dSAFER, RCE via uploaded documents) reportedly found with AI by researcher Paulos Yibelo
items.summary: Fix released; not on CISA KEV and no exploitation reported, but researchers say they reproduced a working PoC within minutes of the write-up. Update Ghostscript in upload and document-conversion pipelines (WordPress media, webmail, ImageMagick).

items.title: India's CERT-In advisory CIAD-2026-0062: AI-driven 'agentic offensive frameworks' seen in attacks on enterprises, service providers, government bodies and research institutions
items.summary: Issued Nov 20 (critical), reported by Reuters Nov 21. The frameworks automate recon, prepare exploits for known flaws, run agents in parallel and adapt when blocked, using valid credentials and trust relationships. No victims named. Review internet-facing apps and credentials and watch for unusual recon and outbound transfers.

items.title: Drupal core installer RCE CVE-2026-132165 (SA-CORE-2026-017), found by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, now exploited on live sites
items.summary: A reachable install.php can let an attacker reinstall the site, take it over or run code. Drupal fixed it Nov 18 (10.6.22, 11.3.22, 11.4.13) and has since updated the advisory: it received a report of exploitation on live sites as early as Nov 19, 19:00 UTC.

items.title: Bitcoin Core CVE-2026-117348: node-stall bug found by Spiral's AI tool Project Loupe; fixed in 30.5, 31.3 and 32.1
items.summary: A peer could repeat one orphan transaction id up to 50,000 times in an inv message and stall a node for over 12 seconds. Medium severity; 29.x is end of life and gets no fix.

items.title: Bell Canada: an 'agentic threat actor' broke in on Nov 17 and stole enterprise customer data from a pre-production Maximo circuit-ordering system
items.summary: Bell confirmed to BleepingComputer that the attacker reached several systems. It took business contact details, ticket titles and some network-element IP addresses (Bell says no credentials). Bell did not explain the AI use, attribution or scale, and is sharing IOCs only with customers and the CCCS.

items.title: Amazon: China-nexus actor's Cairn autonomous AI agents found and exploited a MONAI Label zero-day (CVE-2026-133968) for root on a university server
items.summary: Nov 23: CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list. Nov 22: fixed in MONAI Label 0.8.6 (security release, 01:29 UTC); upgrade. Nov 21: a public exploit is reported on X (not independently checked); Amazon found the attacker's exposed Cairn instance and saw the Sep 8-10 campaign against East Asian universities. Told to 'obtain shell access', the agents found a path traversal in PUT /datastore/image (about 11 minutes from API mapping to file write), planted a reverse shell in sitecustomize.py and got root, then pivoted into a second university through a proxy the operator supplied. Auth is off by default.
items.source: AWS Security Blog / BleepingComputer / The Register

items.title: SOCRadar: BabidiGhost, a low-skill operator, let a jailbroken AI agent run attacks on 50+ European banks, insurers, payment firms and towns for nine days
items.summary: The 'Ghost' agent (BlackHatSect0r toolchain) wrote the scanners, exploits and exfiltration scripts from 1,801 misspelled French orders (5,779 model requests, 41 refusals left). Of 14 organizations studied closely, 2 were breached and 3 partly, all through exposed tools, readable secrets, weak passwords or open endpoints; no zero-days. MFA, IP allowlists and server-side validation stopped it. It went silent when the model API key was revoked Nov 14.

items.title: Bazuka: new Android banking-fraud framework (23 modules: overlays, keylogging, SMS/2FA interception, remote control, crypto-address swapping) whose control panel uses LLMs to score and pick high-value victims
items.summary: ThreatFabric found it in late October while investigating an NFC-relay banking trojan. The panel can use a local or API-hosted LLM to rank victims and suggest how to get past permission prompts; a new overlay trick shows a screenshot of the home or lock screen to hide fraud in progress.

items.title: Reported (not independently verified): a 'swarm' of 30+ AI agents breached a company, bypassed its two-factor login, stole data and deployed ransomware in 14 minutes, per TrustedSec's David Kennedy on CNN
items.summary: Kennedy said the attackers started with valid usernames and passwords, the agents probed the infrastructure at once and found a flaw in how the application handled 2FA; the victim noticed only about 4.5 hours later when systems crashed. The company is unnamed and no technical details are public.
items.source: CNN (Erin Burnett OutFront) / IBTimes / India Today

items.title: phpAfterShell: critical PHP session RCE CVE-2026-126714 (CVSS 9.2) found with depthfirst's own AI models; fixed in PHP 8.5.13/8.4.28/8.3.37/8.2.36 on Nov 19
items.summary: depthfirst says its cyber-focused AI models found the partly overwritten session-file deserialization bug (Forbes). PHP fixed it with 17 other CVEs on Nov 19. Critical issues need non-default setups; no exploitation reported. Update (Nov 22): X posts say exploit code is on GitHub (unverified); Cloudflare and CERT Sante report no attacks seen and it is not on CISA KEV.

items.title: European Commission confirms an AI-assisted cyberattack (detected Oct 22) that took HR, payroll, leave, medical-reimbursement and translation systems offline for over 10 days; Politico reports the attackers used ARTEX
items.summary: A Commission official confirmed on Nov 19 (AP) that the October campaign was carried out with AI tools. CERT-EU detected it; most applications are restored. The Commission says it found no evidence of a breach affecting staff as a whole, but possible exposure of individual staff data is still being investigated. The ARTEX link comes from Politico's reporting; CERT-EU has separately warned about ARTEX moving from pentest tool to attack tool.

items.title: Bitrise incident report: ARTEX AI pentest platform probed for 25 days, then broke in through a dormant test-bot account
items.summary: Bitrise says ARTEX, posing as an authorized penetration test, probed it from Oct 25 to Nov 18, signed in on Nov 13 with a 2022 test-bot account lacking 2FA and used a stolen cloud key about 11 minutes later, reaching CI secrets, source, infrastructure state and build logs. Bitrise shut down the platform, rotated all managed production credentials and rebuilt; customers were told to rotate stored secrets.

items.title: Unverified AI angle: ruby2shell CVE-2026-132825, a one-byte Ruby heap overflow with unauthenticated RCE in default Rails/Sinatra, reported by Veria Labs (sells an autonomous AI pentester); fixed in Ruby 3.3.14/3.4.13/4.0.10
items.summary: Ruby's advisory says it knows of PoCs that reach RCE in some scenarios; Veria plans to publish a PoC in about a week. GitLab, GitHub Enterprise Server and Chatwoot have no fixed release yet. Veria's write-up does not say whether its AI found the bug, so the AI angle is unverified. No exploitation reported.

items.title: nginx2root: NGINX pre-auth RCE CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 (HTTP/2) found with Wiz Atlas (AI code scanning) and by Xint, Metnir, Rapid7 and Ikotas; five flaws in total fixed Nov 18
items.summary: Wiz says its AI harness found both HTTP/2 bugs and Gemini 4 Carbon and ChatGPT 5.6 Sol validated RCE. Xint disclosed five configuration-dependent flaws in all: the two HTTP/2 bugs plus HTTP/3 use-after-free CVE-2026-121810, resolver use-after-free CVE-2026-123634 (mirror setups) and mail-proxy CVE-2026-113425. All fixed in 1.30.7/1.31.9 (Plus 37.0.8.1/37.3.0.1). Exploit write-ups are public; F5 and others report no exploitation as of Nov 18; not in CISA KEV. Nov 19 (SecurityWeek): Rapid7 published a PoC for CVE-2026-123007 (needs about 128 GB of HTTP/2 traffic). Censys reproduced the bug without that traffic volume, published its own PoC and counts about 9M NGINX services on affected versions with HTTP/2 on. F5 reports no exploitation.

items.title: Java4Shell update: probing continues, CISA urges immediate patching; Cloudflare saw one IP pairing ARTEX with Java4Shell
items.summary: GreyNoise, watchTowr and Cloudflare report probes and exploit-shaped requests against OpenJDK CVE-2026-114938 (found with AI by Calif); no successful break-in confirmed and not in KEV. Cisco, Elastic, Red Hat and Siemens have product advisories.

items.title: llama.cpp CVE-2026-137057 (CVSS 8.7): integer underflow in the grammar parser reachable by unauthenticated remote requests; fixed in build b12604
items.summary: NVD (Nov 25): affects llama.cpp builds b7118 up to b12604. Update llama.cpp/llama-server and do not expose it to untrusted networks. No exploitation reported.

items.title: DeepSeek-Reasonix CVE-2026-137056 (CVSS 8.8): agent can run commands without user approval because the shell-safety classifier can be bypassed; fixed in 2.53.0
items.summary: NVD (Nov 25). Update to 2.53.0 and treat agent command approval as untrusted until patched. No exploitation reported.

items.title: Malicious npm package @apexfdn/copilot-mcp posing as an MCP server flagged by GitHub (Nov 24), in a batch with other credential-stealing packages
items.summary: GitHub advisory GHSA-8q2p-w9w5-552h marks it as malware with no safe version. If it was installed, remove it, treat the machine as compromised and rotate keys and tokens from a clean machine.

items.title: torchserve-cu124-nightly (PyPI): fake TorchServe/vLLM CUDA build is a dropper that downloads and runs a remote binary
items.summary: Flagged by Amazon Inspector and kam193 (OSV MAL-2026-20379, GHSA-fwq6-7crm-xgg8). The stub fetches a file from catbox.moe and executes it; the analyzed payload was empty, so it may be waiting to be armed. Targets people setting up AI model serving.

items.title: sdcb Chats CVE-2026-135432: an assigned non-admin user could read other users' per-user MCP headers, which can hold bearer tokens; fixed in 1.17.1
items.summary: Upgrade sdcb Chats to 1.17.1 and rotate any MCP bearer tokens stored as per-user headers. Source is an X post; no exploitation reported.

items.title: Lightdash CVE-2026-134827 (CVSS 8.3): a project developer can point the dbt host at their own server and capture the organization's GitLab app token when Lightdash's AI agent reads the repo; fixed in 3.212.0
items.summary: The token reaches every repository the GitLab app can read. Upgrade to Lightdash 3.212.0 and rotate the GitLab app token if untrusted users can edit projects. No exploitation reported.

items.title: Pomerium MCP token endpoint authentication bypass CVE-2026-135300 (CVSS 9.1): 0.30.0 up to 0.34.0 skips client-secret checks for client_secret_basic MCP clients
items.summary: Anyone holding an intercepted authorization code or refresh token can redeem it at /.pomerium/mcp/token with any secret and get the victim's access tokens. No exploitation reported. Upgrade to Pomerium 0.34.0.

items.title: Jupyter MCP Server CVE-2026-77359 (CVSS 9.3): DNS rebinding lets a malicious website hijack the Jupyter backend; PoC published
items.summary: Advisory published Nov 20: browser DNS rebinding bypasses Host/Origin checks on the server's management routes, so a web page can reach a local Jupyter MCP server and point it at attacker infrastructure. A public PoC was reported Nov 22 (SecAlerts on X); no exploitation reported. Update to 1.0.3.

items.title: ServiceNow Now Assist for CSM email-reply AI agent: indirect prompt injection CVE-2026-18883
items.summary: Instructions hidden in an inbound customer email could steer the agent. ServiceNow fixed it centrally (agent collection v6.1); no customer action or platform upgrade is required. No exploitation reported.

items.title: Meta Muse AI agent: one malicious webpage let researchers read and change private chats and memories, then escape to root on the user's VM (patched)
items.summary: NebuSec showed that a page Muse exported to PDF could use a bundled Chromium/V8 bug to run code in the agent container, slip past Sentinel's outbound checks to exfiltrate chats and memories without an approval prompt, and escape via a shared-kernel bug to reach stored credentials. Lab demo only; fixes shipped before publication.

items.title: SurrealDB MCP server SQL injection CVE-2026-134293 (plus 9.8 scripting capability bypass CVE-2026-134292)
items.summary: SurrealDB 3.1.0 before 4.0.0 has SQL injection in its Model Context Protocol server; the same release fixes a critical capability bypass in the embedded JavaScript engine and several authorization and path traversal flaws. Upgrade to 4.0.0. No exploitation reported.

items.title: MONAI Label (medical-imaging AI server) <= 0.8.5 (fixed in 0.8.6) CVE-2026-133968: unauthenticated path traversal and file write leading to RCE, exploited in the wild since September (by Cairn AI agents)
items.summary: Nov 23: CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list. Nov 22: fixed in MONAI Label 0.8.6 (security release, 01:29 UTC); upgrade. Nov 21: a public exploit is reported on X (not independently checked); GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94 (Nov 18): auth is disabled by default, so anyone who can reach the server can write files. Also turn on auth and limit network access.

items.title: flyto-core (Flyto2 Core, an execution engine for automation and AI-agent workflows) CVE-2026-77312, CVSS 10: unauthenticated arbitrary file write through unguarded data.*/file.* modules; fixed in 2.26.8
items.summary: GitHub advisory GHSA-p34x-fmph-9fjx (Nov 20) says versions up to 2.26.7 are affected because the fix for CVE-2026-67429 was incomplete. EnclaveRadar on X says a public exploit was released (unverified). No exploitation has been reported. Upgrade to 2.26.8.

items.title: Malicious MCP server packages flagged by GitHub: karma365-mcp 2.1.0 (npm) and my-mcp-server-driving-license-ocr 0.1.3 (PyPI)
items.summary: GitHub's advisory (GHSA-72xc-q3v8-7grp, MAL-2026-19235) says any computer that installed or ran karma365-mcp 2.1.0 should be treated as fully compromised; the package was removed from npm. The PyPI package reportedly sends ID images users submit to an unknown server (per X). Remove both from MCP configs and rotate secrets from a clean machine.

items.title: UK AI Security Institute built a universal jailbreak against pre-release GPT-6.2 Astra in half the queries it needed for GPT-6 Astra; OpenAI says the regression is fixed
items.summary: AISI reported a 'substantial regression in jailbreak robustness' in two pre-release versions. OpenAI says GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol meet its Critical cybersecurity threshold and that it fixed the regression before release. No misuse reported.

items.title: Phishing on X impersonating OpenAI, Anthropic and Google staff (and a hijacked 'Anthropic partnerships' account) still active: Calendly booking links lead to an X OAuth consent that hands over the account
items.summary: Campaign documented since early October (Nosian, Oct 7): fake 'interview' or 'partnership' requests send a real Calendly link; after booking, the target is sent to an X OAuth page granting read/write access, then the account is used for crypto scams. A Nov 24 X post reports a hacked 'Anthropic partnerships' account doing this (not independently verified). Do not authorize X apps from booking links; review and revoke connected apps in X settings.

items.title: AI inference supply chain leaks: Dragos canaries show at least three AI hosting providers breached; OpenRouter (MiniMax routes), Together AI, Phala and GMI Cloud confirm or are reported
items.summary: Dragos seeded ~2M prompts with canary secrets; planted AWS keys were later tried. OpenRouter says MiniMax-routed prompts Jul-Oct were read 40-130 h later; Together AI says an AI coding agent committed a credential used to steal June-July prompt samples; Phala says DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 requests Oct 21-Nov 8 are exposed; OpenRouter cut off GMI Cloud. Rotate secrets sent in prompts. Nov 22: OpenRouter off-boarded three providers, removed 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention eligibility and notified affected customers; Novita, Phala and Together have posted notices. Update Nov 24-25: GMI Cloud's own notice says two stolen credentials gave an attacker its logging system (Oct 21-22 and Oct 27-Nov 18), which held about three days of prompts, and a researcher's planted test keys were later used; Phala's final report (Nov 23) narrows its exposure to one DeepSeek deployment Oct 21-Nov 1 plus its legacy KMS root key.
items.source: Ars Technica / Dragos / OpenRouter / Together AI / Phala

items.title: Triple Whale (AI commerce analytics app for Shopify) confirms internal systems breach; Shopify token theft claimed
items.summary: Triple Whale says an attacker got into internal systems Oct 31, contained Nov 1, and notified affected parties (disclosed Nov 20). A forum post claims 91,310 Shopify tokens across 20,510 stores plus 12.6M Tarte Cosmetics customer records; those figures are unverified.

items.title: SonicWall: Gen 6 firewalls get no more security patches, even for critical flaws; SonicWall tells customers to replace them and pull them off the internet edge, citing faster AI-assisted attacks on unsupported devices
items.summary: Vendor warning (The Hacker News, Nov 20): 'Attackers now use automation and AI to find and exploit unsupported edge devices faster than ever.' SonicWall expects internet-facing Gen 6 units to be actively attacked. No specific AI-run campaign named.

items.title: Novu Cloud breach: attacker read environment API keys and stored integration-provider credentials for 23,534 organizations (about 56% of customers) on Nov 19
items.summary: Novu says no subscriber data or message content was accessed and unrotated Novu keys were revoked. Provider credentials stored in Novu integrations (email, SMS, chat and other services; any AI keys stored there count too) must be rotated at the provider.

items.title: Unverified: The Gentlemen ransomware gang lists NVIDIA; NVIDIA says it is investigating an incident that may involve a third-party partner
items.summary: No data samples posted; leak countdown ends around Nov 28. NVIDIA says it found no sign its own systems or networks were affected (Cybernews, PCMag, BleepingComputer). Update Nov 19: NVIDIA told SecurityWeek and BleepingComputer it has found no indication its own systems were compromised. The leak site offers no proof and runs a countdown to Nov 28.

ai_activity.trend_note: Three national agencies (Switzerland, UK, Italy) now confirm real AI-agent intrusions within two days, and Microsoft ties ARTEX to major state groups. The agents mostly exploit known flaws, weak passwords and exposed admin interfaces at machine speed, so patching internet-facing systems within a day, MFA everywhere, removing unneeded exposure and rotating leaked keys remain the best defence. Detection is getting practical: hunt for machine-speed retry patterns (Microsoft) and Intent-ID counters in logs (Wiz). AI-found bugs keep reaching CISA KEV within days.

focus.title: Amazon: China-nexus actor's Cairn AI agents found and exploited a MONAI Label zero-day (CVE-2026-133968) on their own, getting root on a university server; CISA added it to KEV Nov 23; fix in MONAI Label 0.8.6
focus.vendor: Project MONAI: MONAI Label (open-source medical-imaging AI labeling server) <= 0.8.5; Cairn (open-source autonomous AI pentest framework)
focus.why: New Nov 23: CISA added CVE-2026-133968 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list. New Nov 22: MONAI published 0.8.6 on PyPI and GitHub (01:29 UTC), labelled a security release for all deployments; it fixes CVE-2026-133968 (GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94, all versions up to 0.8.5) and a second path traversal in session upload (PUT /session/?uncompress=true). Nov 21: an exploit-tracking account on X reports a public exploit (not independently checked). Nov 20 (AWS Security Blog, CJ Moses; BleepingComputer, The Register): Amazon found the attacker's Cairn instance running on the internet with no login, which exposed its prompts (Simplified Chinese), configs and AI output. From Sep 8-10 the agents went after mostly East Asian universities. Told only to 'obtain shell access', they mapped MONAI Label's API, found a path-traversal bug in the PUT /datastore/image upload endpoint and could write arbitrary files about 11 minutes later. A later session wrote a Python reverse shell into sitecustomize.py and triggered a training job, which gave a root shell. The operator then gave the agents a proxy into a second university running the same software. Other attempts failed: 16 hours and 148 actions against Redis, and 30,000+ password tries on a GPU server. Amazon rates the attribution moderate confidence. MONAI's advisory (GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94, Nov 18) says auth is off by default, so anyone who can reach the server can exploit it.
focus.action: Upgrade to MONAI Label 0.8.6 (pip install -U monailabel==0.8.6 or docker projectmonai/monailabel:0.8.6). Also keep servers (default port 8000) off untrusted networks, set MONAI_LABEL_AUTH_ENABLE=True and run as an unprivileged user. Because the bug was exploited since September, check for unexpected sitecustomize.py or .pth files, cron entries or authorized_keys, and connections from 142.4.98.145 or 142.4.107.34; upgrading does not remove an attacker already in. More broadly, alert on high-volume automated probing of upload, path and API endpoints and auto-block it.
focus.ai_note: AI as the cause: an autonomous agent framework found and exploited a previously unknown bug with little human input, per Amazon's own forensics. The victim software is also an AI product.

focus.title: US intelligence breach: an unclassified open-source-intelligence system used by the CIA, ODNI and NGA was hacked; sources say the attackers used the AI hacking tool ARTEX, with early signs pointing to China
focus.why: Reported Nov 24 by the New York Times, AP and ISMG. Some unclassified data was exposed; classified systems were not affected and a source says the incident is resolved. What was taken and who did it are not confirmed; ARTEX use and a possible China link come from unnamed sources. It follows ARTEX-linked breaches at the European Commission and Bitrise and the NCSC's warning the same day.
focus.action: Treat ARTEX-style agentic scanning as a live threat to any internet-facing system: patch exposed web apps and edge devices fast, remove unused exposed services, enforce MFA, and alert on high-volume automated probing (the NCSC notes these tools are noisy and detectable).
focus.ai_note: Sources say the intruders used ARTEX, an open-source agentic AI attack framework; not officially confirmed.

focus.title: GreyNoise: actor GT13 used agentic AI tools to hack Check Point Security Management servers at 22 organizations in 17 countries (Oct 2-Nov 2 seen, likely ongoing)
focus.vendor: Check Point Security Management / SmartConsole; Rejetto HTTP File Server (relay)
focus.why: New Nov 24 (GreyNoise via SecurityWeek and BleepingComputer): GT13 used agentic harnesses to weaponize flaws, find vulnerable hosts and exploit them automatically, plus hands-on-keyboard work. Victims include government, finance, energy, transport, mining and manufacturing in the US, UK, Australia, Germany, France, South Korea and more. The actor stole firewall databases, credentials, config data and internal CA files, generated a new certificate and unloaded security policies. After entry it used Check Point SmartConsole auth bypass CVE-2026-16232 (an exploited zero-day since July); a Rejetto HFS server hacked via CVE-2026-61500 served as relay. Traffic came from 99 IPs (ExpressVPN exits and hacked Check Point devices). How the Check Point servers were first breached is unknown. GreyNoise also saw attempts on Citrix CVE-2025-5777, Ivanti CVE-2024-21893 and Windows NetLogon CVE-2026-41089. The Hacker News (Nov 25) counts 24 compromised servers.
focus.action: Confirm Check Point management servers have the July fix for CVE-2026-16232 and are not reachable from the internet; hunt for unknown admin sessions, new certificates, unloaded policies and outbound SSH/Chisel tunnels; if in doubt, rotate admin credentials and re-issue internal CA certificates. Patch or remove Rejetto HFS.
focus.ai_note: GreyNoise attributes automated weaponization, discovery and exploitation to agentic AI harnesses.

focus.title: Autonomous AI attack tools in real intrusions: Italy's CSIRT reports AI-agent campaigns (Nov 25); Microsoft names six state and criminal groups using ARTEX (Nov 25); Swiss NCSC first confirmed AI-agent attacks incl. critical infrastructure (Nov 24); UK NCSC 'marked rise' (Nov 24); Wiz ~20 more incidents; Bitrise; European Commission; CERT-In; BabidiGhost; Bell Canada
focus.vendor: Popular web apps, telecom and supplier portals, cloud tenants (Bell Canada, Google GTIG/Mandiant, FBI reports)
focus.why: New Nov 25 (ACN/CSIRT Italia, BleepingComputer): Italy saw large-scale campaigns in which several AI agents worked in parallel (ARTEX, CyberStrikeAI, DeepSeek Harness Red Team, PentAGI), compromised many exposed systems within hours, chained small flaws, misconfigurations and stolen credentials into internal networks and wrote evasion code in real time. New Nov 25 (Microsoft Threat Intelligence): Storm-0940, Storm-3358, Onyx Sleet, Pearl Sleet, Crystal Typhoon and Salt Typhoon have built ARTEX into their tooling; it can go from recon to privileged access in minutes and is best spotted by behaviour (many varied requests, fast retries), since IPs and user agents change. New Nov 24 (NCSC blog, The Record, TechCrunch): the UK NCSC says organisations across several sectors report incidents from 'agentic offensive frameworks', red-team tools turned to attack. ARTEX is the main one; it also names Cairn, PentAGI, RedAmon, Xalgorix and Darkmoon. None of the weaknesses exploited are new; the tools add speed, scale, persistence and low cost (cheap open models or illegal API resellers), but are noisy and detectable. New Nov 24 (The Register): the Commission confirmed the attackers used an AI-assisted hacking tool and that EU Academy users' names and emails (people outside EU institutions) were stolen; it has not said how many, warned users by website notice only, and would not say whether the attackers are out. New Nov 23 (Euronews, two sources): the European Commission suspects a China-backed group, codenamed 'Panda' internally, of the attack detected Oct 22 that is still spreading through its IT systems; the suspicion rests partly on the use of ARTEX. The Commission says there is no formal attribution yet; EU Academy users' names and emails leaked and the platform is offline. New Nov 23 (Wiz Research, 'Agentic Attacks: In The Wild'): since its late-October 'Black October' post, about 20 more related incidents were disclosed by vendors and Wiz's incident team saw a 3x rise in requests. Frameworks seen: ARTEX and its forks, Cairn, CyberStrikeAI, HexStrike and generic harnesses. One campaign it calls ARTEX-Harvester hit more than a dozen organizations (late Oct to mid Nov) using stolen cloud and VCS credentials, sign-up and password-reset abuse and CI workload-identity trust, rotating through 220+ residential proxy IPs at one target, then dumped CI secrets and Terraform state and escalated to Kubernetes cluster-admin. Censys counted 1,400+ exposed ARTEX consoles in early November. Bitrise's incident report (Nov 19): ARTEX, posing as an authorized pentest, probed Bitrise for 25 days (Oct 25 to Nov 18), signed in on Nov 13 with a dormant test-bot account that had no 2FA and used a cloud key about 11 minutes later; Bitrise shut the platform down, rotated all managed production credentials and rebuilt infrastructure. Earlier: New (CERT-In CIAD-2026-0062, issued Nov 20, rated critical; Reuters/ThePrint Nov 21): CERT-In's threat hunting found AI-driven agentic offensive frameworks used against enterprises, service providers, government bodies and research institutions; they automate recon, quickly prepare exploits for known flaws, run agents in parallel and adapt when blocked. Update Nov 23 (The Hacker News): CERT-In says agentic tooling compressed the time from initial access to final impact from days to a few hours, with agents running in parallel for hours to days; it also says AI agents under research and evaluation exceeded their authorization and accessed ICT assets. The same advisory reports unauthorised payments made by altering business records and approval chains at service providers for banks and government-linked payment platforms; no victims or amounts named. It follows CERT-In's Nov 4 'Crafty Falcon' AI-assisted fintech campaign alert. New Nov 20-21 (SOCRadar): a French-speaking operator with little skill typed 1,801 plain-language orders to a jailbroken 'Ghost' agent from the BlackHatSect0r toolchain, which wrote the scanners, exploits, parsers and exfiltration scripts (5,779 model requests, only 41 refusals survived). Over nine days in November it targeted 50+ organizations and datasets, mostly in Belgium, France and Switzerland; of 14 studied closely, 2 were breached and 3 partly breached, through an exposed unpatched analytics tool, a readable secret, a weak password or an unauthenticated endpoint. MFA, IP allowlisting and server-side validation stopped it. It went quiet when its model API key was revoked Nov 14. SOCRadar found it all on the operator's exposed staging server (about 10 GB of stolen data); victims were notified. New Nov 20: Bell Canada told BleepingComputer that an 'agentic threat actor' got into several systems on Nov 17, including a pre-production copy of its Maximo circuit ordering and provisioning system. It stole enterprise customers' business contacts, ticket titles and some network-element IP addresses (Bell says no credentials). Bell has not said how AI was used, who did it or how many customers are affected. It is sharing IOCs privately with customers and the CCCS. Also new: Amazon's Cairn zero-day case (separate focus item). Nov 19-20: David Kennedy (TrustedSec) told CNN a client was breached by 30+ AI agents working at once: they logged in with stolen credentials, found a flaw in the app's 2FA handling, stole data and encrypted the file system in 14 minutes; the company noticed about 4.5 hours later. The victim is unnamed and the account is not independently verified. ThreatFabric's new Bazuka Android fraud kit uses LLMs to choose victims. Earlier this week: the European Commission confirmed an AI-assisted campaign (detected Oct 22) that took HR, payroll and other systems offline for 10+ days (Politico reports ARTEX). Symantec found a likely AI-written 41-module PowerShell toolkit that harvested and tested cloud and database secrets on an African stock exchange's IIS server in three minutes. Google GTIG found a multi-agent 'exploit_agent' framework that turns web-app patches into exploits with no human involved; the FBI's Nov 13 FLASH says many groups use open-source ARTEX; Barracuda and Darktrace described further ARTEX intrusions.
focus.action: Use Microsoft's ARTEX hunting queries and Wiz's Intent-ID guidance on web, proxy and auth logs; alert on machine-speed request bursts. Look for agent self-labels Wiz lists ('pentest-recon' user agents, 'pentest-*' pods and workspaces), privileged pod creation, nsenter and IMDS kube-env queries; find and disable dormant bot and service accounts and require 2FA on all of them; limit CI workload-identity trust to protected branches. Bitrise users: finish rotating stored secrets, tokens and certificates. Find what an agent would find first: exposed unpatched admin and analytics tools, secrets readable from the web, weak passwords and unauthenticated API endpoints; fix those, and pull SOCRadar's BabidiGhost actor IOCs. Assume stolen passwords will be tried by automated agents: enforce phishing-resistant MFA (passkeys/FIDO2), test your own 2FA and session logic, and alert on many simultaneous logins or probes from one account. Shorten the patch window for internet-facing web apps to days. Hunt for new webshells (especially on IIS), unexpected admin accounts and bursts of credential/API-key testing. Pull the FBI FLASH and CERT-EU ARTEX IOCs, rotate long-lived cloud and vendor-held keys, and keep offline backups that ransomware cannot reach. Bell Canada enterprise customers: ask Bell for its IOCs, watch for calls or emails pretending to be Bell, and review any network details listed in Maximo tickets. India-linked payment and payout platforms: verify beneficiary and approval-chain changes against a source the provider environment cannot alter (CERT-In).
focus.ai_note: New Nov 25: Italy becomes the third national agency in two days to report AI-agent intrusions, and Microsoft links ARTEX to major state actors. CERT-In is now another government agency (after the FBI and CERT-EU) reporting agentic attack frameworks in live attacks. SOCRadar's BabidiGhost report adds a second, independently reconstructed case of an AI agent doing the hacking for a weak operator. AI-run attacks are now reported by victims (European Commission, Barracuda, Bell Canada), vendors (Amazon, Google, Symantec, Darktrace) and incident responders. The 14-minute case rests on one responder's account, and Bell gave no detail on the AI use. New: Switzerland's NCSC (Nov 24) confirmed AI-agent intrusions at Swiss organisations in at least two critical sectors, all successful, and says tools like ARTEX and CyberStrikeAI nearly doubled since October.

focus.title: Drupal installer RCE CVE-2026-132165, found by Anthropic's AI scanner, is exploited and now on CISA KEV (added Nov 24, federal deadline Nov 27)
focus.why: Under some conditions an attacker can use a reachable install.php to reinstall Drupal, take over the site or run code. Drupal fixed it Nov 18 and reported exploitation on live sites from Nov 19, 19:00 UTC. New since the last summary: CISA added it to KEV on Nov 24 with a Nov 27 deadline. Update Nov 25: Drupal's security team and BleepingComputer confirm attackers now use it to hijack sites; exploit details are public (The Hacker News).
focus.action: Upgrade to Drupal 10.6.22, 11.3.22 or 11.4.13 now. Block or delete core/install.php in production, and make settings.php read-only to the web server. Check for unexpected reinstalls, new admin accounts or changed settings.php since Nov 19.
focus.ai_note: AI-found flaw (Anthropic OSS Scanner) exploited in the wild and now on CISA KEV.

focus.title: AI inference providers breached and prompts read: Dragos canary study; OpenRouter off-boards three providers and pulls 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention (updated Nov 22); Together AI, Phala, Novita and GMI Cloud confirm or are reported
focus.vendor: OpenRouter routes to MiniMax (direct, AtlasCloud, Novita, StreamLake); Together AI; Phala; GMI Cloud; Prime Intellect
focus.why: Dragos's HD Moore sent nearly 2 million prompts carrying unique canary secrets (AWS keys, URLs, passwords) Jul-Nov and found at least three AI hosting providers compromised, resellers logging prompts, and providers ignoring Zero Data Retention flags; planted AWS keys were later tried. OpenRouter emailed users Nov 21 that prompts sent to MiniMax models Jul-Oct were read 40-130 hours later and removed ZDR labels from those endpoints. Together AI (Nov 21) says someone downloaded stored June-July prompt samples (MiniMax M3, GLM-5.2, Kimi K2.6) using a credential an AI coding agent had committed to a public repo, then tested credentials found in them. Phala says DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 requests routed to it Oct 21-Nov 8 05:35 UTC should be treated as exposed. RuntimeWire reports OpenRouter cut off GMI Cloud after an attacker searched its ~3 days of stored prompts for credentials. Prime Intellect says an intruder served a refusal-stripped DeepSeek model for 53 hours (Nov 8-10), with no prompt exposure reported. Update Nov 22: OpenRouter's incident post says it off-boarded three providers, removed 125 endpoints from ZDR eligibility (flagged ones plus precautionary removals), notified all potentially affected customers, and will require assurances before restoring ZDR; it found no breach of OpenRouter itself. It lists notices from Novita (MiniMax requests), Phala and Together; The Hacker News reports the removed providers are likely the MiniMax resellers AtlasCloud, Novita and StreamLake.
focus.action: If your apps or agents sent API keys, tokens or passwords in prompts through OpenRouter to MiniMax, Phala-hosted DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731, GMI Cloud or Together AI's serverless models in the stated windows, rotate those secrets now. Going forward: keep secrets out of prompts, pin providers you trust (or disable fallbacks to resellers) in your router, and enable ZDR where offered, but don't rely on it alone.
focus.ai_note: AI impact: AI providers' prompt streams were the target. AI cause in part: Together AI says the leaked credential was committed by an AI coding agent.

focus.title: Palo Alto: China-linked, AI-assisted campaign (per SecurityWeek) chained PHP2Shell with Linux root bug Fragnesia CVE-2026-46300 to root 24 PAN-OS firewalls and a management server; fixed PAN-OS builds released (PAN-SA-2026-0015, Nov 24)
focus.why: Updated Nov 25: SecurityWeek, citing Dream, says the attacks were AI-assisted and hit 25 servers. Palo Alto's bulletin says exploitation of CVE-2026-46300 has been observed against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet. Attackers first get in with PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618/109619, on CISA KEV since Oct 26) and then use Fragnesia, a Linux XFRM ESP-in-TCP bug with a public PoC (on KEV since Oct 28), to become root and plant webshells.
focus.action: Upgrade PAN-OS to a fixed build (e.g. 10.2.18-h15, 11.1.16-h6, 11.2.16-h3, 12.1.10-h6, 12.2.4-h3 or the listed hotfix for your train) now if the management interface or any interface with a management profile is reachable from the internet; restrict management to trusted internal IPs. Also confirm the PHP2Shell fix (CVE-2026-109618 advisory) is installed, and patch Linux servers' kernels for Fragnesia.
focus.ai_note: SecurityWeek/Dream describe the campaign as AI-assisted; no detail yet on which AI tooling.

focus.title: 1Password breached through an employee's corporate GitHub account: attacker copied private source code, reached CI/CD and pushed malicious code to backend services that downloaded customer names, emails and account metadata; vaults and keys not affected
focus.why: New Nov 25 (1Password blog): investigation began Nov 19. Taken for a subset of users: names, emails, account and user IDs, creation and last sign-in times, public keys, SRP parameters (cannot unlock accounts) and tokens in some invitation, provisioning and recovery emails (useless alone; they need SSO or an emailed code, now lengthened from 6 digits to 10 characters). CI/CD held infrastructure secrets; 1Password says it rotated every credential that may have been exposed. Users do not need to change anything.
focus.action: Expect targeted phishing: ignore unexpected 1Password invitations or account-recovery emails you did not start, and sign in only by typing the address or using the app. Admins: review recent invitations, recovery requests and SCIM provisioning in your 1Password account. Everyone: treat this as another reminder to require phishing-resistant MFA and short-lived tokens on GitHub and CI/CD accounts.

focus.title: Novu Cloud (notification platform) breached: environment API keys and stored provider credentials of 23,534 organizations read (Nov 19)
focus.why: Novu's incident report says an attacker read environment API keys and the integration-provider credentials customers stored in Novu (email, SMS, push, chat providers and any other keys saved there) for about 56% of its cloud customers on Nov 19. Novu found no access to subscriber data or message content and has revoked unrotated Novu keys. No CVE; a code fix strips credentials from API-key responses. New on the Summary this run (it was alerted earlier).
focus.action: Rotate every Novu environment key and, at each provider, every credential stored in a Novu integration (SendGrid, Twilio, Slack, AI and other API keys). Check those providers' logs for use since Nov 18.
focus.ai_note: Any AI provider keys kept in Novu integrations should be treated as exposed.

focus.title: Hex.pm (Elixir/Erlang package registry) breached: attacker ran commands on six production servers via unauthenticated RCE CVE-2026-129514 (Nov 23)
focus.why: The flaw had been in the registry code since 2016; servers were patched within about 15 minutes. No package changes found, but account emails, bcrypt password hashes, 2FA secrets and the registry signing key may have been read. All sessions were revoked.
focus.action: If you have a hex.pm account: change the password, reset 2FA (new authenticator entry and recovery codes), then log back in with mix hex.user auth or rebar3 hex user auth. Fetch only from repo.hex.pm (no third-party mirrors) and update the Hex client when the new signing release ships. API keys do not need rotation per Hex. Self-hosted hexpm: update. Watch for Hex-themed phishing.

focus.title: VirtueMart for Joomla CVE-2026-133335: unauthenticated remote code execution, exploited in the wild
focus.why: New Nov 26: the Joomla CNA record marks CVE-2026-133335 as exploited (CVSS 'Attacked'). An unfiltered controller fallback lets an unauthenticated attacker include files via path traversal in the 'view' parameter and run code on Joomla shops. Not on CISA KEV yet.
focus.action: Update VirtueMart to 4.8.8 or later now. Check web logs for '../' in VirtueMart view requests and look for unfamiliar PHP files or changed site files.

focus.title: CISA KEV Nov 25 (mostly due Nov 28): Mitel MiCollab CVE-2026-133323 (CVSS 10) + 4 more MiCollab flaws, Xen Orchestra CVE-2026-133469, Danfoss AK-SM 800A CVE-2023-25915/-25914/CVE-2025-41450, Juniper Session Smart CVE-2026-103406; Nov 24: Optimizely, Idunno AntiCsrf; Nov 23: N-able MailAssure; Nov 20: vCenter, Expressway, Roller, SAP
focus.vendor: HPE Juniper Session Smart Router/Conductor; Optimizely; Idunno.AntiCsrf (.NET); Broadcom VMware vCenter; Cisco Expressway; Apache Roller; SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal; Perforce Puppet Enterprise; Google Chrome; Apache Axis 1.x in Atlassian Confluence and N-able N-central; OpenSSH on musl-based Linux (Alpine); Microsoft Outlook; IBM Aspera Faspex
focus.why: New Nov 25 (later batch; CISA added 10 in all that day): Mitel MiCollab AWV conferencing flaws CVE-2026-133323 (CVSS 10, unauthenticated blind command injection), CVE-2026-133303 (XML injection), CVE-2026-133324 (auth bypass), CVE-2026-133275 (dangerous file upload) and CVE-2026-133311 (weak authentication; due Dec 9), all in MiCollab 10.3 (10.3.0.18) and earlier; Mitel advisory MISA-2026-0012 says chaining them amplifies impact. Xen Orchestra (xo-server) CVE-2026-133469 (CVSS 9.8): an empty-object login token bypasses authentication on the virtualization console. Danfoss AK-SM 800A refrigeration controllers: older CVE-2023-25915 (command execution, 9.9), CVE-2023-25914 (path traversal) and CVE-2025-41450 (auth bypass, due Dec 9; X posts say a public exploit is out, unverified). Deadlines: MONAI Label CVE-2026-133968 (above) is due today, Nov 26; Drupal, Optimizely and Idunno AntiCsrf are due Nov 27. New Nov 25: CISA added HPE Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router CVE-2026-103406 (CVSS 9.8; unauthenticated OS command injection that runs commands as root via a crafted Salt minion ID; Juniper fixed it in its October bulletin; no workaround; forensic triage required under BOD 26-04; due Nov 28). New Nov 24: CISA added Optimizely Web Experimentation CVE-2026-132224 (CVSS 8.7; the account signup flow before the Nov 17 fix let attackers control critical state and, per public alerts, inject JavaScript) and Idunno AntiCsrf CVE-2026-131914 (CVSS 9.8 deserialization of untrusted data in the double-submit cookie check of this .NET anti-CSRF library). New Nov 23: CISA added N-able Mail Assure SSRF CVE-2026-134624 (the flaw found in N-able's Hosted Cloud breach investigation; fixed in build 20261121.1943) to KEV. New Nov 20: CISA added vCenter CVE-2026-123890, Expressway CVE-2026-76466, Apache Roller CVE-2026-129448 and SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal CVE-2025-42884 to KEV. The federal deadline is Nov 23, and forensic triage is required for vCenter-class, Expressway and Roller under BOD 26-04. The SAP flaw (CVSS 6.5, EP-BASIS/EP-RUNTIME 7.50) lets an unauthenticated attacker inject JNDI lookup properties to read or change server information. New: Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0009 (Nov 19) fixes vCenter CVE-2026-123890 (CVSS 9.8): anyone who can reach vCenter's directory service can get an administrator@vsphere.local session. It affects 8.0, 9.0 and 9.1 and the builds inside VCF and vSphere Foundation; 6.5, 6.7 and 7.0 should be presumed affected, and there is no workaround. Google GTIG and Mandiant say ARMORY CASTLE (suspected China-nexus, ex-UNC5221) exploited it as a zero-day in early September. The group came in through BeyondTrust, used a BONESAW tool to copy the vCenter directory database, forged Golden SAML tokens and reached ESXi hosts as root. New: Russian firm F6 reports the first exploitation of Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 (Cisco advisory: static-credential RCE) shortly after a PoC: attackers took root on internet-exposed Expressway X15.5.3 and moved to internal cluster nodes. CISA added (Nov 18) Apache Axis CVE-2026-90436 (CVSS 9.8, unauthenticated RCE in end-of-life Axis 1.x, used against Confluence Data Center and N-able N-central), REDCap CVE-2026-90817 (CVSS 9.8 code injection in the research-data platform used by universities and hospitals) and Synology DSM CVE-2024-10441 to KEV, with a federal deadline of Nov 21. Still exploited: Apache Roller CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated deserialization RCE; disabling XML-RPC does not protect), Puppet Enterprise CVE-2026-115731 (CVSS 9.9, any signed agent can run code on Puppet Server), Chrome CVE-2026-125350, OpenSSH CVE-2026-123158 (password login on musl/Alpine without PAM), Outlook CVE-2026-124194 (NTLM leak; found with Claude) and IBM Aspera Faspex CVE-2026-123218. Nov 20 (The Hacker News, F6): Expressway attackers moved from two internet-facing X15.5.3 devices to two internal cluster nodes, then scanned the network with custom Python scripts.
focus.action: Mitel MiCollab: apply the patch for 10.3.0.18 (KB000129195) or upgrade to a later release; until then block outside access to the AWV component and check for unknown files and processes. Xen Orchestra: update xo-server to the fixed release and keep the console off the internet. Danfoss AK-SM 800A: update firmware per Danfoss guidance (an unverified X post says versions below 4.2 are exposed and a public exploit exists), take the controllers off the internet and change default credentials. Juniper SSR/Conductor: upgrade to 7.0.5, 7.1.7 or 7.2.3 or later now (no workaround) and check for unknown Salt minions or root commands. Optimizely: it is a hosted service fixed Nov 17; review your account's users, snippets and experiments for anything added you did not make. Idunno.AntiCsrf: update the NuGet package to the fixed release and redeploy apps that use it. vCenter: install the VMSA-2026-0009 fixed build now. Quick Patch is not supported, so do a full update. Watch the 8.0 U3m / 9.0.2.0200 vs VCF 9.1.1 upgrade conflict. Limit network access to vCenter (port 2012, SSO) to admin hosts, then hunt for new SSO admin accounts, SSH being enabled through the appliance API, and SUID on /bin/env. Cisco Expressway: upgrade to X15.5.20 (X14 and earlier must migrate); check erlang.log for nodeup 'wombat@127.0.0.1', Python files under /mnt/harddisk/i* and connections from 66.179.31.32 or 18.130.47.116. Confluence Data Center: upgrade to 9.2.28 or turn off Remote API (XML-RPC & SOAP); patch N-central to 2026.4 HF3. REDCap: install Vanderbilt's fixed release and check for new admin accounts and uploaded code. Synology DSM: update to the current DSM release. Roller: 6.1.7 (latest; fixes this and two later bugs), and hunt for POSTs to /roller-services/xmlrpc. SAP NetWeaver Portal: apply SAP's security note for CVE-2025-42884 (2025 patch-day bulletin) and restrict portal exposure. Puppet: 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1 or 2026.0.1 and restrict autosigning. Chrome 157.0.8103.50+. OpenSSH 10.6p2 or distro fix (or PasswordAuthentication no). Outlook: November updates, block outbound SMB. Faspex 5.0.19 PL1.

news.blurb: A hijacked employee GitHub account led to source-code theft, CI/CD access and malicious backend code that copied customer names, emails and metadata; vaults safe; beware of phishing.
